title: Biodiversity and Classification
seo_title: Grade 10 Life Sciences: Biodiversity and Classification Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_code: Grade 10 Life Sciences: Biodiversity and classification
standard_text: Biodiversity; classification schemes and the history of classification; the five kingdoms and three domains; the hierarchy of taxonomic categories; binomial nomenclature; dichotomous keys; South Africa as a mega-diverse country. (summary of CAPS Life Sciences, Grade 10, Life Sciences: Biodiversity and classification)
meta_desc: Free Grade 10 Life Sciences worksheets (CAPS): biodiversity, kingdoms and domains, taxonomic ranks, binomial names and dichotomous keys. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Scientific names have two parts: genus and species.
key_sub: Kingdom → phylum → class → order → family → genus → species.
body_html:
How to think about it

Biodiversity is the variety of life. South Africa is one of the most biodiverse countries in the world. Organisms are classified into groups by shared features: three domains (Bacteria, Archaea, Eukarya) and five kingdoms (Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia).

The taxonomic ranks are kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus and species. Each species has a binomial name written in italics, for example Panthera leo (lion): the genus starts with a capital letter. Dichotomous keys identify organisms using pairs of choices.

Example

In Panthera leo, which word is the genus?

The first word

Answer: Panthera

Example

Which kingdom do mushrooms belong to?

They do not photosynthesise.

Answer: Fungi

Common mistakes

  • Writing the species name with a capital letter.
  • Thinking fungi are plants.
  • Mixing up the order of the ranks.

faq.q: Why are scientific names better than common names?
faq.a: Each species has one unique name used all over the world.

faq.q: What makes a group of organisms one species?
faq.a: They can interbreed and produce fertile offspring.

items.q: What does the IUCN Red List record?
c: the conservation status of species and those threatened with extinction
items.e: Updated regularly.

items.q: Which population is most at risk from a new disease?
c: a population of a widespread species
a large population with many alleles
a small, inbred population with low genetic diversity
items.e: Tasmanian devils have low genetic diversity, which helped facial tumour disease spread.

items.q: What does ‘ecosystem services’ mean?
c: the benefits people get from ecosystems, such as clean water, pollination and food
money paid to visit a national park
the number of species in an ecosystem
items.e: Mangroves protect coasts and act as fish nurseries.

items.q: Why should we conserve biodiversity?
c: for food, medicines and other products, for ecosystem services, and for ethical reasons
items.e: Amazon forests make a lot of oxygen.

items.q: Why was the Nile perch harmful in Lake Victoria?
c: it led to the extinction of more than 200 species of cichlid fish
items.e: An example of alien species invasion.

items.q: What is ecosystem diversity?
c: the size of the largest ecosystem
the number of species in one quadrat
the variety of alleles in one species
the variety of habitats, communities and ecological processes in a region
items.e: A region with reef, mangrove and seagrass has high ecosystem diversity.

items.q: What is species diversity?
c: the number of individuals of one species
the number of species in an area and how evenly the individuals are spread among them
the variety of alleles in a population
the variety of ecosystems in a region
items.e: Species diversity takes in richness and evenness.

items.q: What is species evenness?
c: the number of individuals of the rarest species
the total biomass of the community
how similar the population sizes of the different species are
items.e: A community where one species dominates has low evenness.

items.q: What is genetic diversity?
c: the variety of alleles and genes within a species
the number of different species in an area
the variety of habitats in a region
the number of individuals in a population
items.e: Genetic diversity is variation inside one species.

items.q: What is co-extinction?
c: the extinction of a species that depends on another species that has become extinct
the birth of a new species
items.e: e.g. a parasite dying with its host.

items.q: Why is high genetic diversity important to a population?
c: it increases the population's size immediately
some individuals are more likely to survive a new disease or change
items.e: Variation is the raw material for natural selection.

items.q: What does the 'rivet popper' hypothesis say?
c: losing species is like removing rivets from a plane: losing key ones can make the ecosystem collapse
items.e: Proposed by Paul Ehrlich.

items.q: Two sites each have 5 species. At site An each species has about 20 individuals; at site B one species has 90 and the rest have 2 or 3. Which is more diverse?
c: site B, because it has more individuals of one species
site A, because it has the same richness and higher evenness
they are equally diverse because richness is the same
site B, because dominance means a healthier community
items.e: Same richness, higher evenness = higher diversity.

items.q: Which is an ecosystem service of mangroves?
c: protecting coastlines from erosion and providing nurseries for fish
producing most of the oxygen for cities
items.e: Mangrove roots trap sediment and shelter young fish.

items.q: What does the species–area relationship of Alexander von Humboldt state?
c: species richness increases with area, but only up to a limit
items.e: log S = log C + Z log A.

items.q: Tasmanian devils have very low genetic diversity. Why has this made devil facial tumour disease worse?
c: the disease is caused by a mutation in the climate
low diversity makes them grow too fast
their immune systems do not recognise tumour cells from other devils as foreign
items.e: Similar genes mean the tumour cells are not rejected.

items.q: What is species richness?
c: how evenly individuals are spread among species
the number of different species in an area
items.e: Richness counts species; evenness compares their numbers.

items.q: What is the most species-rich group of animals?
items.e: More than 70% of all recorded animal species.

items.q: How does species diversity change from the equator to the poles?
c: it is highest at the poles
items.e: The tropics are the richest.

items.q: What is biodiversity?
c: the total mass of plants in an ecosystem
the variety of life at the genetic, species and ecosystem levels
the number of endangered species in a country
the number of animals in an area
items.e: Biodiversity includes genetic, species and ecosystem diversity.

items.q: What does a dichotomous key do?
c: lists organisms in order of size
measures the size of a population
shows how energy flows through an ecosystem
identifies organisms by a series of choices between two features
items.e: Each step splits the group into two.

items.q: In the hierarchy of classification, which taxon comes directly below genus?
items.e: Domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.

items.q: In the hierarchy of classification, which taxon comes directly above family?
items.e: Domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.

items.q: Which feature is best for a dichotomous key?
c: its colour after it has died
the time of day the organism was seen
a feature that does not change, such as number of legs
items.e: Use features that are fixed and easy to observe.

items.q: A cladogram shows that zebras and lions share a more recent common ancestor than zebras and platypuses. What does this mean?
c: zebras are more closely related to lions than to platypuses
zebras and platypuses are the same species
items.e: A more recent common ancestor means a closer relationship.

items.q: Which domain includes many organisms that live in extreme environments such as hot springs?
items.e: Archaea are prokaryotes but differ from bacteria in their membranes and rRNA.

items.q: What is the common name of Pisum sativum?
items.e: Pisum sativum: pea.

items.q: Which definition of a species is used for organisms that reproduce sexually?
c: a group that can interbreed in nature to produce fertile offspring
a group of organisms that look the same
a group of organisms with the same diet
all organisms that live in one habitat
items.e: This is the biological species concept.

items.q: Which statement about classification is correct?
c: organisms in the same kingdom are always the same species
organisms in the same genus are more closely related than organisms in the same order
a class is smaller than a genus
items.e: Lower taxa share more features.

items.q: Why is DNA sequencing now used to classify organisms?
c: it is cheaper than looking at organisms
it shows relationships that are hidden by similar or different body shapes
it removes the need for names
items.e: Convergent evolution can make unrelated organisms look alike.

items.q: In the hierarchy of classification, which taxon comes directly above genus?
items.e: Domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.

items.q: What is the correct order of taxa from largest to smallest?
c: domain, kingdom, class, phylum, family, order, genus, species
domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species
kingdom, domain, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species
species, genus, family, order, class, phylum, kingdom, domain
items.e: Each taxon is nested inside the one above.

items.q: Which is the scientific name for human?
items.e: Homo sapiens: human.

items.q: What feature defines marsupials?
c: young are born very small and usually develop in a pouch
they have a long placental pregnancy
items.e: Zebras, lions and meerkats are marsupials.

items.q: In the hierarchy of classification, which taxon comes directly below family?
items.e: Domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.

items.q: Which is the scientific name for housefly?
items.e: Musca domestica: housefly.

items.q: A horse and a donkey produce a mule, which is sterile. What does this show?
c: donkeys are a subspecies of horse
horses and donkeys are separate species
horses and donkeys are the same species
items.e: Hybrids are not fertile, so the parents are different species.

items.q: What is the common name of Gossypium hirsutum?
items.e: Gossypium hirsutum: cotton.

items.q: What are the three domains of life?
items.e: The three-domain system is based on rRNA sequences.

items.q: Which domain includes all organisms with a nucleus?
items.e: Animals, plants, fungi and protists are eukaryotes.

items.q: Which is the scientific name for cat?
items.e: Felis catus: cat.

items.q: Why is growth not a defining property of living things?
c: non-living things such as mountains and crystals can also grow by accumulation
items.e: Growth in living things is from inside.

items.q: A quadrat survey found: species A 2, species B 10, species C 8, species D 12, species E 3. Calculate Simpson's index of diversity, D = 1 − Σn(n − 1)/N(N − 1).
What is the common name of Felis catus?
items.e: Felis catus: cat.

items.q: In the hierarchy of classification, which taxon comes directly above phylum?
items.e: Domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.

items.q: A quadrat survey found: species A 20, species B 20, species C 3, species D 2, species E 20. Calculate Simpson's index of diversity, D = 1 − Σn(n − 1)/N(N − 1).
In the hierarchy of classification, which taxon comes directly above class?
items.e: Domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.

items.q: A quadrat survey found: species A 10, species B 12, species C 5, species D 5. Calculate Simpson's index of diversity, D = 1 − Σn(n − 1)/N(N − 1).
A quadrat survey found: species A 12, species B 5, species C 12, species D 3, species E 2. Calculate Simpson's index of diversity, D = 1 − Σn(n − 1)/N(N − 1).
In the hierarchy of classification, which taxon comes directly below order?
items.e: Domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.

items.q: What is the common name of Musca domestica?
items.e: Musca domestica: housefly.

items.q: A quadrat survey found: species A 12, species B 5, species C 8. Calculate Simpson's index of diversity, D = 1 − Σn(n − 1)/N(N − 1).
In the hierarchy of classification, which taxon comes directly below kingdom?
items.e: Domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.

items.q: In the hierarchy of classification, which taxon comes directly above kingdom?
items.e: Domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.

items.q: A quadrat survey found: species A 10, species B 2, species C 15, species D 4. Calculate Simpson's index of diversity, D = 1 − Σn(n − 1)/N(N − 1).
What is the common name of Oryza sativa?
items.e: Oryza sativa: rice.

items.q: Which is the scientific name for mango?
items.e: Mangifera indica: mango.

items.q: Which is the scientific name for pea?
items.e: Pisum sativum: pea.

items.q: What is the common name of Panthera tigris?
items.e: Panthera tigris: tiger.

items.q: Which is the scientific name for dog?
items.e: Canis familiaris: dog.

items.q: Which taxonomic aid is a garden of living plants grown and labelled for study?
items.e: botanical garden: a garden of living plants grown and labelled for study.

items.q: Which category includes related orders?
items.e: e.g. Mammalia includes Primata and Carnivora.

items.q: Why are fungi called saprophytes?
c: they absorb food from dead and decaying matter
items.e: They are important decomposers.

items.q: Which kingdom has members that are multicellular eukaryotes with no cell wall that ingest food?
items.e: Animalia: multicellular eukaryotes with no cell wall that ingest food.

items.q: Who proposed the five-kingdom classification?
items.e: Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia (1969).

items.q: Which description fits kingdom Fungi?
c: prokaryotic, mostly unicellular, with a cell wall of peptidoglycan
heterotrophic eukaryotes with a cell wall of chitin
multicellular eukaryotes with no cell wall that ingest food
items.e: Fungi: heterotrophic eukaryotes with a cell wall of chitin.

items.q: Which kingdom has members that are euglenoids, with a pellicle and a flagellum?
items.e: Euglena photosynthesises in light.

items.q: What are viroids?
c: free RNA without a protein coat that cause disease
items.e: Found by T. O. Diener; cause potato spindle tuber disease.

items.q: In Mangifera indica, what does 'indica' stand for?
items.e: Mangifera is the genus.

items.q: Which taxonomic aid is a store of pressed, dried and labelled plant specimens on sheets?
items.e: herbarium: a store of pressed, dried and labelled plant specimens on sheets.

items.q: Which kingdom has members that are heterotrophic eukaryotes with a cell wall of chitin?
items.e: Fungi: heterotrophic eukaryotes with a cell wall of chitin.

items.q: What are heterocysts in cyanobacteria used for?
items.e: e.g. Nostoc and Anabaena.

items.q: What is a herbarium?
c: a garden of living plants grown and labelled for study
an account of the plant species found in an area
a store of pressed, dried and labelled plant specimens on sheets
a book that helps identify the species in an area
items.e: herbarium: a store of pressed, dried and labelled plant specimens on sheets.

items.q: What is the main drawback of the two-kingdom classification?
c: it puts prokaryotes and eukaryotes, unicellular and multicellular, together
items.e: Bacteria, fungi and plants were all in Plantae.

items.q: Which kingdom has members that are multicellular eukaryotes with a cellulose cell wall that make their own food?
items.e: Plantae: multicellular eukaryotes with a cellulose cell wall that make their own food.

items.q: What is the genetic material of bacteriophages usually?
items.e: Plant viruses usually have single-stranded RNA.

items.q: Which description fits kingdom Protista?
c: heterotrophic eukaryotes with a cell wall of chitin
multicellular eukaryotes with no cell wall that ingest food
prokaryotic, mostly unicellular, with a cell wall of peptidoglycan
items.e: Protista: unicellular eukaryotes.

items.q: Which kingdom has members that are prokaryotic, mostly unicellular, with a cell wall of peptidoglycan?
items.e: Monera: prokaryotic, mostly unicellular, with a cell wall of peptidoglycan.

items.q: Which protists cause red tides?
items.e: They can release toxins that kill fish.

items.q: Which description fits kingdom Monera?
c: heterotrophic eukaryotes with a cell wall of chitin
multicellular eukaryotes with a cellulose cell wall that make their own food
prokaryotic, mostly unicellular, with a cell wall of peptidoglycan
items.e: Monera: prokaryotic, mostly unicellular, with a cell wall of peptidoglycan.

items.q: Which feature is typical of phylum Platyhelminthes?
c: a stomochord and proboscis gland, as in Balanoglossus
a water vascular system and spiny skin
items.e: Platyhelminthes: flat bodies and flame cells.

items.q: Which phylum has a water vascular system for movement and feeding?
items.e: It moves by many small water-filled tubes (podia).

items.e: Porifera: the cellular level of organisation.

items.q: Which description fits kingdom Animalia?
c: multicellular eukaryotes with no cell wall that ingest food
heterotrophic eukaryotes with a cell wall of chitin
prokaryotic, mostly unicellular, with a cell wall of peptidoglycan
items.e: Animalia: multicellular eukaryotes with no cell wall that ingest food.

items.q: What is metagenesis?
c: alternation between polyp and medusa forms
items.e: e.g. Obelia.

items.q: Which feature is typical of phylum Annelida?
c: the tissue level of organisation and cnidoblasts (stinging cells)
items.e: Annelida: metameric segmentation and nephridia.

Which site in Daniel's survey is likely to recover better from a disease that kills one species?
c: site B, because it has more individuals
site A, because it has more species
items.e: More diverse ecosystems are more stable.

items.q: Which animals are diploblastic?
items.e: They have only ectoderm and endoderm.

items.q: Which kingdom has members that are unicellular eukaryotes?
items.e: Protista: unicellular eukaryotes.

items.q: Which animals show radial symmetry as adults?
items.e: Echinoderm larvae are bilaterally symmetrical.

items.q: Which feature is typical of phylum Hemichordata?
c: a stomochord and proboscis gland, as in Balanoglossus
a soft body covered by a calcareous shell and a mantle
a water vascular system and spiny skin
items.e: Hemichordata: a stomochord and proboscis gland, as in Balanoglossus.

items.q: Which phylum shows a soft body covered by a calcareous shell and a mantle?
items.e: Mollusca: a soft body covered by a calcareous shell and a mantle.

items.q: Sea otters eat sea urchins, which eat kelp. Otters disappear. What is the most likely result?
c: Many new wetland species can live there.
Mussels take over and fewer species remain.
Urchins increase and kelp forests shrink.
items.e: A keystone species has a large effect.

items.q: A disease kills most of the starfish on a rocky shore. What is the most likely result?
c: Many new wetland species can live there.
Mussels take over and fewer species remain.
Urchins increase and kelp forests shrink.
items.e: A keystone species has a large effect.

items.q: Which animals have flame cells for excretion?
items.e: Flame cells also help in osmoregulation.

items.q: What is a lichen?
c: a symbiotic association of an alga and a fungus
items.e: They are pollution indicators.

items.q: Which phylum shows a water vascular system and spiny skin?
items.e: Echinodermata: a water vascular system and spiny skin.
